STOPS.name: Route 66 Breakfast
STOPS.blurb: Griddles, coffee and a sink full of dishes.

STOPS.name: Drive-In Burgers
STOPS.blurb: Hot fryers, cold shakes and a lot of patties.

STOPS.name: Texas BBQ Smokehouse
STOPS.blurb: Low and slow. Get the smokers going before the orders come in.

STOPS.name: Tex-Mex Border Town
STOPS.blurb: Every order is built their way. Read the ticket carefully.

STOPS.name: New Orleans Cajun
STOPS.blurb: Big pots, and everything goes in the right order.

STOPS.name: New York Deli & Pizza
STOPS.blurb: Stretch it, top it, bake it, slice it.

STOPS.name: New England Seafood Shack
STOPS.blurb: Chowder, fish & chips, and lobsters that will not sit still.

STOPS.name: California Coast
STOPS.blurb: Fresh, fast and impatient. Short cooks, shorter tickets.

STOPS.name: Thanksgiving Finale
STOPS.blurb: The end of the road. Everyone is coming for dinner.

STOPS.name: The Judge's Table
STOPS.blurb: One service. One judge. No mercy.

STOPS.name: Roadside Specials
STOPS.blurb: Bonus kitchens off the main road. Stars from anywhere on the trip open them.

LEVELS.name: Salad Days
LEVELS.tip: Take lettuce from its crate, drop it on a board and chop. Put it on a plate and serve at the bell.

LEVELS.name: Soup Kitchen
LEVELS.tip: Put three chopped tomatoes or three chopped onions in a pot. When it dings, pour it onto a plate. If you leave it too long it catches fire: pick up the extinguisher and hold Spray.

LEVELS.name: The Divide
LEVELS.tip: The kitchen is split in two. Chop on one side, pass food over the middle counter and cook on the other. Tap Swap to switch chefs.

LEVELS.name: Dinner Rush
LEVELS.tip: Everything is on the menu. Get a pot going first, then chop while it cooks.

LEVELS.name: Sunrise Griddle
LEVELS.tip: Put eggs, bacon and batter straight on a griddle, and take them off before they burn. Dirty plates come back through the hatch: carry them to the sink and hold Wash.

LEVELS.name: Bottomless Coffee
LEVELS.tip: Tap Grab on a coffee machine to brew a mug. Coffee is served in the mug, so it needs no plate.

LEVELS.name: Truck Stop Rush
LEVELS.tip: The Big Breakfast needs a pancake, an egg and bacon on one plate. Keep all three griddles busy.

LEVELS.name: Curb Service
LEVELS.tip: Chop potatoes and drop them in the fryer. Patties now cook on the griddle too. Fryers burn fast, so stay close to them. New: delivery tickets have a paper bag on them. Plate the order, tap Grab at the bag station, then hand the bag off at the pickup window before the driver leaves.

LEVELS.name: Shake Shack
LEVELS.tip: Put a scoop of ice cream in a blender (add a strawberry for a pink one) and tap Blend. Shakes go out in the cup, with no plate.

LEVELS.name: Friday Night Rush
LEVELS.tip: Chop and plate on the left, fry, grill and blend on the right. Pass food over the counter, and keep an eye on those fryers. Bag delivery tickets and hand them off at the window.

LEVELS.name: Low & Slow
LEVELS.tip: Ribs take a long time in the smoker, so load them before the orders arrive. Smoked meat keeps once it is off the heat. Cornbread goes on the griddle.

LEVELS.name: Brisket Board
LEVELS.tip: Smoked brisket has to be sliced on a board before it goes on a plate. Mac & cheese: two macaroni and one cheese in a pot.

LEVELS.name: Pitmaster Showdown
LEVELS.tip: The Pitmaster Platter needs ribs, sliced brisket and cornbread on one plate. Keep all three smokers full.

LEVELS.name: Taco Truck
LEVELS.tip: Every ticket lists its own toppings. Warm a tortilla on the griddle, add the meat, then exactly the toppings shown. Extra toppings pay more, and a wrong build gets sent back. Delivery tickets go in a bag and out the pickup window.

LEVELS.name: Burrito Bar
LEVELS.tip: Burritos need rice and beans. Each takes two scoops in its own pot. Keep both pots going and chop avocado for guacamole.

LEVELS.name: Fiesta Night
LEVELS.tip: Everything, all built to order. Build and serve on the left, cook on the right, and read every ticket.

LEVELS.name: Bayou Kitchen
LEVELS.tip: Gumbo goes in the pot in order: onion, then sausage, then shrimp. The ticket shows the order. Beignets are dough fried in the fryer, then dusted with sugar on the plate.

LEVELS.name: Jazz Brunch
LEVELS.tip: Jambalaya: rice first, then sausage, then tomato. Both stews share sausage, so chop plenty.

LEVELS.name: Mardi Gras
LEVELS.tip: Chop on the left, stew and fry on the right. Three pots and two fryers: keep them all moving.

LEVELS.name: Corner Slice
LEVELS.tip: Stretch dough on a board, then add sauce, then cheese (then pepperoni if the ticket shows it). Bake it in the oven, then slice it on a board. Pizza delivery! Bag the slices for delivery tickets.

LEVELS.name: Deli Counter
LEVELS.tip: Pastrami gets sliced on a board, then goes on rye with mustard. Bagels toast in the oven. Add cream cheese straight from the tub.

LEVELS.name: Midtown Lunch Rush
LEVELS.tip: Build pizzas on the left and bake them on the right. Keep the ovens full and slice as fast as you can. Office delivery orders: bag them for the window.

LEVELS.name: Harbor Shack
LEVELS.tip: Chowder: shucked clams, chopped potato and milk in a pot. Fish & chips: fillet the fish on a board and fry it, then fry the chips.

LEVELS.name: Lobster Pound
LEVELS.tip: Lobsters are alive! Leave one on a counter and it scuttles off, and from an edge it can escape for good. Carry it straight to a pot, then serve it in a roll.

LEVELS.name: Nor'easter
LEVELS.tip: The whole shack at once, split down the middle. Pass the lobsters across fast, before they walk off.

LEVELS.name: Venice Beach
LEVELS.tip: California tickets are short and come fast. Fish grills in seconds on the griddle, and so does toast. Read each taco ticket for its toppings.

LEVELS.name: Smoothie Stand
LEVELS.tip: Smoothie bowl: blend a banana with a strawberry, pour it into a bowl (onto a plate), then top it with granola.

LEVELS.name: Sunset Rush
LEVELS.tip: Everything on the coast, split in two, and the tickets keep coming. Keep the griddles and blenders busy. Delivery tickets: bag and hand off at the window.

LEVELS.name: Family Dinner
LEVELS.tip: The turkey takes a long time in the oven, so get it in early. Carve it on a board. Mash: two chopped potatoes and milk in a pot. Pies bake, then get sliced.

LEVELS.name: Grandma's Kitchen
LEVELS.tip: The Feast is carved turkey, stuffing and mash on one plate. Stuffing: chopped bread and onion in a pot.

LEVELS.name: The Big Feast
LEVELS.tip: The last service of the road trip: five minutes, the whole family, and every oven and pot you have. Good luck, chef.

LEVELS.name: The Judge's Table
LEVELS.note: All judges are fictional parody characters, not affiliated with or endorsed by any real chef.
LEVELS.tip: Judges Nyesha Garnishton, Richard Braise and Yourdone Ramsey taste everything. Three strikes and you are out: a wrong dish, cold food (more than 15 seconds off the heat), overcooked food, anything burning, or a customer who gives up waiting. Tickets are shorter here. Plate it hot, and plate it right.

LEVELS.name: Midnight Diner
LEVELS.tip: Open all night: big breakfasts, cheeseburgers, fries and bottomless coffee from one kitchen.

LEVELS.name: State Fair
LEVELS.tip: If it holds still, fry it. Three fryers, a blender and the longest line at the fair.

LEVELS.name: Ghost Kitchen
LEVELS.tip: No dining room and no bell. Every ticket is a delivery: bag it and hand it to a driver at one of the two windows.

start: Welcome to MY kitchen. Three mistakes and you are OUT.
Every plate crosses this pass. Every. Single. One.
wrong: That is NOT what they ordered! Read the ticket!
Did you even LOOK at the ticket?
Wrong dish! Are you cooking blindfolded?
late: The customer LEFT. Can you blame them?
Too slow! They grew a beard waiting!
out: Three strikes. You are DONE. Get out of my kitchen!
That is it. Apron off. You are DONE!
pass: ...Fine. You can cook. Now get out before I change my mind.
overcooked: Overcooked! This is charcoal with a garnish!
That heat was way too high, chef. Dry as a desert!
Science says no. That protein is ruined!
burn: I smell smoke! Get that off the heat!
You burnt it! Watch your pans!
That is not a sear, that is a crime scene!
cold: It is cold. Temperature is everything, chef!
This plate went cold on the pass. Serve it hot!
Cold food tells me you were not ready. Be ready.

ramsey: Good. Now do it again. Faster.
spark: Now THAT is a perfect cook!
Beautiful sear. The science checks out.
ember: Lovely. Hot, fresh and on time.
That is a plate I would serve. Well done.

chop.name: Prep Cook
chop.blurb: Chops, slices and stretches anything left on a board.

fryer.name: Fry Cook
fryer.blurb: Pulls food out of the fryer before it burns.

griddle.name: Grill Cook
griddle.blurb: Takes food off the griddle before it burns.

stove.name: Pot Watcher
stove.blurb: Moves finished pots and pans off the stove.

smoker.name: Pitmaster
smoker.blurb: Pulls meat out of the smoker when it is done.

oven.name: Baker
oven.blurb: Takes pizzas, pies and roasts out of the oven.

sink.name: Dishwasher
sink.blurb: Brings dirty plates to the sink and washes them.

GEAR.name: Tip Jar Apron
GEAR.text: +8% tips on dishes this chef serves

GEAR.name: Waiter's Apron
GEAR.text: Walking +7% while carrying a plate or cup

GEAR.name: Oven Mitts
GEAR.text: Food this chef puts on the heat takes 8% longer to burn

GEAR.name: Fire Gloves
GEAR.text: Puts out fires 7% faster, with slightly longer reach

UPGRADES.name: Safety Fryer
UPGRADES.text: Fryer food takes 25% longer to burn

UPGRADES.name: Non-Stick Griddle
UPGRADES.text: Griddle food takes 25% longer to burn

UPGRADES.name: Heavy Pots
UPGRADES.text: Pots and pans take 25% longer to burn

UPGRADES.name: Stone Oven
UPGRADES.text: Oven food takes 25% longer to burn

UPGRADES.name: Street Performer
UPGRADES.text: A busker plays to the line outside: customers wait 10% longer

UPGRADES.name: Grippy Tyres
UPGRADES.text: Better grip; drifts are easier to control

lines: Forty years I ran this diner. Now the old food truck is fixed up and the road is calling.
Rosa says if we can run her kitchen, we can run any kitchen in America.
Learn the basics here. Then we drive.
Route 66! Truckers want breakfast, and they want it hot.
And somebody has to wash the plates. Welcome to dishes.
A drive-in! Burgers, fries and shakes under the neon.
Watch that fryer. I am not buying another fire extinguisher.
Folks want food brought out to their cars too. Bag it and I will run it.
I have none. Good thing the smoker does.
Everyone here orders their own way. Extra cheese, no lettuce, you name it.
So read the ticket. Every topping, every time.
New Orleans. My mother’s gumbo: onion first, then sausage, then shrimp.
And if I put the shrimp in first?
Then you are walking to New York.
New York! Pizza by the slice and pastrami piled high.
New Yorkers do not wait. Neither do we.
Rosa, the lobsters keep climbing out of the crate!
Short cooks and short tempers. Keep it fresh and keep it moving.
Last stop. The whole family is coming for Thanksgiving dinner.
All of it at once? Turkey, stuffing, mash and pie?
All of it. Let’s bring it home.
Rosa, there is a letter. Three famous chefs want to taste our food.
The Judge’s Table. Nobody passes the Judge’s Table.

TUT_STEPS.text: Welcome to the kitchen! Drag anywhere on the left half of the screen to walk your chef around.

An order just came in. The picture on the ticket is the dish, and the icons under it are what goes in it. This one is just lettuce. The bar shrinks while the customer waits. Tap a ticket any time to see it bigger.
Walk up to the lettuce crate and tap Grab. White corners show what you’re facing.
Face a chopping board and tap Grab to put the lettuce down.
Tap Chop. Your chef keeps chopping until the green bar fills up.
Grab a clean plate from the stack. You can carry one thing at a time.
Bring the plate to the chopped lettuce and tap Grab to put it on the plate.
Now take the plate to the bell (that’s the serving pass) and tap Grab to serve it.
Order up! Every dish earns coins, plus a tip for serving it fast. Your total is shown up here.
You have two chefs. Tap Swap to switch to the other one, so one can chop while the other plates.
This ticket needs lettuce and tomato on one plate. Chop both, plate them together, and serve. Swap whenever it helps.
Made a mistake? Carry anything to the bin to throw it away. Plates and pots just get emptied.
Watch for these signs while you cook:
icons: Fire! Grab the extinguisher and hold Spray

TUT_STEPS.text: That’s the basics. Every new kitchen shows a card explaining its new equipment. Now off to the Hometown Diner!

DAILY_TWISTS.name: Short-Staffed
DAILY_TWISTS.blurb: Only one of your chefs turned up today (solo play).

DRIVE_RUNS.name: Drive-In Strip
DRIVE_RUNS.blurb: A roomy town to learn in: lighter traffic and a couple of road works.

DRIVE_RUNS.name: Big Easy Streets
DRIVE_RUNS.blurb: Busy streets, crowded sidewalks and road works everywhere.

DRIVE_RUNS.name: Manhattan Rush
DRIVE_RUNS.blurb: A huge grid, bumper-to-bumper traffic and people everywhere.

DRIVE_TUT.text: Drag up on the left side of the screen to drive forward.
Drag left or right to steer. Turn at the next corner.
Now get some speed, then drag down to brake and come to a stop.
Drift: at speed, hold the Drift button and steer to slide round a corner. A long slide pays coins.
Follow the green arrow (and the green dot on the map) to the customer. Stop inside the green ring to hand the bag over.
Cones, hydrants and bins pay a coin when you knock them over. People don’t: hitting someone costs 10 coins.
Watch for road works, crashes, potholes and oil. When your bags run out, go back to the truck to reload. The clock starts when you tap Go!
